Analyst Estimates: Here's What Brokers Think Of Ferrari N.V. (BIT:RACE) After Its Third-Quarter Report
sum: It's been a good week for Ferrari N.V. (BIT:RACE) shareholders, because the company has just released its latest quarterly results, and the shares gained 5.6% to €377. The result was positive overall - although revenues of €1.9b were in line with what the analysts predicted, Ferrari surprised by delivering a statutory profit of €2.44 per share, modestly greater than expected. Following the result, the analysts have updated their earnings model, and it would be good to know whether they think there's been a strong change in the company's prospects, or if it's business as usual. We've gathered the most recent statutory forecasts to see whether the analysts have changed their earnings models, following these results.

Taking into account the latest results, the current consensus from Ferrari's 21 analysts is for revenues of €8.27b in 2027. This would reflect a notable 10% increase on its revenue over the past 12 months. Per-share earnings are expected to leap 26% to €11.07. In the lead-up to this report, the analysts had been modelling revenues of €8.27b and earnings per share (EPS) of €11.04 in 2027. So it's pretty clear that, although the analysts have updated their estimates, there's been no major change in expectations for the business following the latest results.

There were no changes to revenue or earnings estimates or the price target of €393, suggesting that the company has met expectations in its recent result. There's another way to think about price targets though, and that's to look at the range of price targets put forward by analysts, because a wide range of estimates could suggest a diverse view on possible outcomes for the business. There are some variant perceptions on Ferrari, with the most bullish analyst valuing it at €435 and the most bearish at €330 per share. This is a very narrow spread of estimates, implying either that Ferrari is an easy company to value, or - more likely - the analysts are relying heavily on some key assumptions.
Looking at the bigger picture now, one of the ways we can make sense of these forecasts is to see how they measure up against both past performance and industry growth estimates.

Haas F1 Driver Ollie Bearman Shares What Keeps Him in the Fast Lane
sum: British racing driver Ollie Bearman has had a passion for cars for as long as he can remember. “I fell in love with racing when I was very young, pushing little model cars around the living room. My dad raced at the club level, and I fell in love with it watching him,” he recalls. “After the first time I rode in a go-kart, it was clear that that was my calling and what I wanted to do.”

Bearman stepped behind the wheel at age seven in competitive kart racing, racking up national and continental titles, before graduating to the world of formula racing in his early teens. In 2022, he joined the Ferrari Driver Academy, where he became a reserve driver for Ferrari and Haas’ Formula 1 teams. In 2024, at 18, he made his Formula 1 debut, substituting for Ferrari driver Carlos Sainz Jr. in the Saudi Arabian Grand Prix. The following year, he joined the Haas F1 Team as a full-time driver, a group he’ll compete with this November during the Formula 1 Las Vegas Grand Prix.

“It’s a cool circuit because it’s a place that I never thought that Formula 1 would be racing at growing up,” says Bearman of the Vegas competition. “There are a lot of drivers who have been asking for a Vegas Grand Prix, and I competed in my first season in Formula 1, so in that sense I consider myself very lucky. I think it’s a crazy, crazy place and a pretty impressive and unique opportunity to race a Formula 1 car down those famous streets.”

As he completes his second full-time season with Formula 1, Bearman continues to be grateful for how far he’s come. “My dad is a big source of inspiration for me. He’s worked incredibly hard to get me to where I am; he funded my career all the way up until Ferrari came along and started helping me out,” he reflects. “He and the rest of my family have made a huge sacrifice to allow me to be in the position I am today.”
Here, Bearman shares the essentials that help him put the pedal to the metal.

sum: Mumbai: India's benchmark stock indices, Sensex and Nifty, saw a significant surge in early trading on Monday. The positive ...

Foreign capital inflows and a positive trend in Asian markets further supported the upbeat sentiment. The BSE Sensex rose by 764.72 points to reach 75,216.80, while the NSE Nifty gained 201.40 points, hitting 23,255.90.

Among the 30 Sensex companies, Reliance Industries was a standout performer. The company reported a record profit of ₹29,550 crore for the July-September quarter, a substantial 33.8 percent increase year-on-year. Other gainers included NTPC, Tata Steel, Power Grid, Maruti, and State Bank of India. Conversely, Sun Pharma, Tech Mahindra, Titan, and Infosys saw their shares decline.

Globally, Asian markets like South Korea's Kospi, Japan's Nikkei 225, China's SSE Composite, and Hong Kong's Hang Seng traded higher. This comes despite US markets closing significantly lower on Friday. Brent crude oil, an international benchmark, slipped three percent to $110 per barrel in futures trading.

Foreign institutional investors (FIIs) were net buyers on Friday, acquiring shares worth ₹3,598.54 crore. On the previous trading day, Sensex had closed 308.49 points higher, and Nifty rose by 116.35 points to finish at 23,053.10.

Antonelli shares touching reaction to ‘incredible’ title win
sum: ‘This moment will live forever’ – Antonelli shares touching reaction to ‘incredible’ World Championship victory in Mexico City
Kimi Antonelli won his maiden Drivers’ Championship with a third-place finish at the Mexico City Grand Prix, leaving him emotional as he reacted to his momentous achievement.

Kimi Antonelli has reacted to winning his maiden World Championship at the Mexico City Grand Prix, with the Italian hiding none of his emotions as he thanked those around him for an “incredible season”.

Although it was Red Bull’s Max Verstappen who won the race ahead of Lewis Hamilton, Antonelli’s P3 finish earned him more than enough points to clinch the title, joining the likes of the Ferrari driver, Graham Hill, and Denny Hulme in doing so at this circuit.

After starting from fourth on the grid, the 20-year-old improved to the top three via a bold overtake on Ferrari’s Charles Leclerc, which allowed him to celebrate his historic victory on the podium after embracing his family and Mercedes team members.

“We did it,” Antonelli said after the race. “You know, without them, I wouldn’t be here – without Mercedes, without my family. So I’m very grateful for this moment, and it’s one that will live forever. I’m speechless. I’m trying to process what has just happened.
“It’s been an incredible season, and to share this podium with Max and Lewis is truly incredible. And yeah, looking forward to some more battles in the future.

items.t: Ferrari's Q1 decision could open the door to an alternative strategy for Hamilton
sum: Lewis Hamilton is the only driver among the frontrunning teams to have fresh soft tyres instead of new medium tyres heading into the Hungarian Grand Prix.

In Q1, Ferrari had already made a strategic decision. Hamilton and Charles Leclerc completed their laps on the medium tyres to secure their places in Q2. However, the Monegasque also had to use the set of soft tyres the team had hoped to save.

As a result, Hamilton is the only driver among the frontrunning teams with a fresh set of soft tyres available instead of a fresh set of mediums for the Hungarian Grand Prix. None of Ferrari's rivals - Mercedes, McLaren or Red Bull Racing - are in the same position.

All four teams also have two new sets of hard tyres at their disposal, making them well placed to follow Pirelli's preferred two-stop strategy: start on the medium tyres before switching to two sets of hards.

According to the Italian manufacturer, a one-stop strategy is also possible if drivers can delay their pit stop until laps 26–32. Using all three tyre compounds is another option, with the longest stint coming on the hard tyres.

Starting on the soft tyres can also give drivers an advantage. Pirelli revealed that, over the distance it takes a car to reach 150 km/h, a driver starting on the soft tyres gains 2.09 metres compared to one starting on the mediums.

Macquarie boss’s shareholding stands out from the crowd
sum: Even by the eye-popping standards of chief executive pay, the riches amassed by Macquarie’s top bankers are exceptional.

When Macquarie Group chief executive Shemara Wikramanayake departs in November, she does so with about $370 million in shares, the fruits of a four-decade career with the investment banking giant. She has another $89 million in deferred share units which are yet to vest.

While it’s difficult to compare executive payouts, each with unique share packages, short-term incentives and bonuses, Wikramanayake will leave Macquarie with one of the most valuable stakes held by a CEO who is not a founder in Australian corporate history.
Founders such as Fortescue’s Andrew Forrest or WiseTech’s Richard White hold stakes in their companies worth billions.

But over the past few years, several high-profile corporate leaders have left the companies they were leading with hefty packages. Virgin boss Jayne Hrdlicka, who left the airline last June, was on track to collect around $50 million based on shares she retained in the company.

Budget jewellery retailer Lovisa raised eyebrows last year when departing chief executive Victor Herrero left with a $39.5 million pay packet, despite the group not even cracking the top 100 companies by market valuation.

After last year’s annual general meeting, where Lovisa shareholders delivered a fifth straight strike against the company’s remuneration report, Monaco-based billionaire owner Brett Blundy likened it to a Ferrari.
